CLUBS AND Wraparound care
Cranford Primary School and our friends at OHM provide a Breakfast Club and a variety of After-School Clubs to offer affordable childcare beyond regular school hours.
Wraparound care can have a positive impact on children’s outcomes in school. Research also shows those who participate in sports, like sports activities during wraparound care, display improved performance and social skills. There are many benefits and impacts of wraparound care for children, parents, and schools.
The Early Birds Breakfast Club is a fantastic way to prepare pupils for the start of the school day. Breakfast Club welcomes pupils from Reception to Year 6 and opens at 7.30am every morning. Pupils have access to a healthy breakfast, including cereal, toast, fresh fruit and juice. Breakfast Club is run by an experienced staff team from OHM. For just £6 a day, students receive a nutritious breakfast and can engage in various art, sport and mindful activities before school begins. By fostering healthy eating habits, the Early Birds Breakfast Club helps students incorporate these practices into their daily lives.
Our After-School Clubs programme encourages children to develop skills in a variety of sports and to broaden their range of experiences and interests as well as helping parents to balance their work and family commitments.
For additional support on childcare costs, please contact the school office on 020 8759 0305 or use the links below:
You can get up to £500 every 3 months (up to £2,000 a year) for each of your children to help with the costs of childcare. This goes up to £1,000 every 3 months if a child is disabled (up to £4,000 a year). Visit: Tax-Free Childcare.
You may be able to claim back up to 85% of your childcare costs if you’re eligible for Universal Credit. Check here.
Childcare choices: https://www.childcarechoices.gov.uk/
Childcare calculator: https://www.gov.uk/childcare-calculator
Parent information Toolkit: https://www.childcarechoices.gov.uk/guidance-and-resources

Meet our school Governors
Our Governing Body
Welcome to the Governing Body pages of our website. My name is Noorian Riaz and I am the Chair of the Governing Body at Cranford Primary School.
Governors work alongside school staff and take decisions affecting the strategic direction of the school. Governors act as ‘critical friends’ and are responsible for holding the school to account and support the school in its endeavour to achieve excellence in all aspects of school life.
Our Governing Body consists of 12 Governors:
1 LA Governor (Chair of Governors)
Nominated by the LA and appointed by the Governing Body
Elected by other members of the Governing Body
Ex Officio by virtue of office as Headteacher
Elected by the parents and must be themselves parents or carers of children who attend the school at the time of the elections. All parents have the opportunity to vote at these elections.
Mrs Sharanjit Dhaliwal
Elected by a ballot of all teachers
Miss Kiranjot Khabra
7 Co-opted Governors
Elected by other members of the Governing Body because of their links with the local community or their particular skills and knowledge
Committee Structure
The full Governing Body meets at least once a term. It has two working committees who report back to the Governing Body at the main meetings. The two committees are:
Curriculum Committee
Membership:
Finance, Staffing, Premises and Health and Safety Committee: Mrs Chana, Mrs Haroon (Chair), Ms Riaz, Mrs D'Lima, Mr Gill
Curriculum Committee: Mrs Mulhair, Miss Khabra, Mrs Tomkins (Chair), Mrs Dhaliwal, Mr Aujla,

pageCache.text:
SEND and Inclusion at Cranford Primary School
At Cranford Primary School, inclusion is at the heart of everything we do. We believe that every child has the right to feel valued, included and successful, and we are committed to ensuring that all pupils are able to access high-quality learning, participate fully in school life and achieve their potential.
We recognise that every child is unique. Some children may need additional or different support at particular points in their school journey, including pupils with Special Educational Needs and/or Disabilities (SEND). Our approach is centred on high expectations, early identification and removing barriers to learning, while developing children's confidence, independence and ability to advocate for themselves.
Our SENDCo is Baljit Santa, who can be contacted through the school office on 020 8759 0305 or office@cranfordprimary.com.”
Our approach to SEND
We aim to identify children's needs as early as possible and work in partnership with pupils, parents and carers to understand the support that will help them thrive.
Our teachers are responsible for the progress and development of every pupil in their class. Through high-quality, inclusive teaching, appropriate adaptations and carefully planned support, we aim to ensure that children with SEND learn alongside their peers wherever possible.
Where a child requires additional support, we use the Assess, Plan, Do, Review cycle to understand their needs, put appropriate provision in place and evaluate its impact. Where necessary, we work closely with external professionals and services to provide more specialist advice and support.
Inclusion at CPS
Our commitment to inclusion extends beyond SEND. We recognise and respond to the individual needs and circumstances of all our pupils, including those who may experience barriers to learning, participation, attendance or wellbeing.
We are committed to creating a school where difference is understood, respected and celebrated and where every child has a strong sense of belonging.
We work to ensure that children:
are supported to achieve ambitious outcomes.
Working in partnership with families
Parents and carers know their children best, and we believe that strong partnerships between home and school are essential.
We encourage families to speak to us if they have concerns about their child's learning, development or wellbeing. We will listen carefully, work collaboratively and agree appropriate next steps.
Our SEND Information Report provides further information about how we identify and support pupils with SEND, the provision available at CPS and how families can access additional advice and support.
At CPS, inclusion means more than simply being present. It means belonging, participating, being heard and having the opportunity to succeed.

Knowledge Organisers
'Knowledge Organisers' are the ‘go-to’ documents outlining all of the essential knowledge that the teachers will be covering across each unit of work including dates, key personnel, vocabulary, definitions and other important information.
Knowledge Organisers remind the children what they are learning and help them see the bigger learning journey as they continually revisit and retrieve prior learning from their memories.
Please refer to these documents with your child - they will assist in homework tasks and improve your child’s knowledge around all of the learning being taught in school.

Safeguarding
At Cranford Primary School, the safety, wellbeing and welfare of every child is our highest priority. We are committed to providing a safe, nurturing and inclusive environment where children feel secure, valued and confident to speak to a trusted adult if they are worried about anything.
Safeguarding is everyone’s responsibility. All members of staff receive regular safeguarding training and understand their responsibility to recognise, respond to and report concerns about a child’s welfare. We work closely with families and, where appropriate, external agencies to ensure children receive the right support at the right time.
Our safeguarding practice is underpinned by the latest Keeping Children Safe in Education (KCSIE) guidance and other relevant statutory requirements. We have clear procedures in place for child protection, safer recruitment, online safety, attendance, behaviour and the management of concerns or allegations.
Worried about a child?
If you have a concern about the safety or wellbeing of a child at Cranford Primary School, please contact the school and ask to speak to a member of our Designated Safeguarding Team.
Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL): Mrs Jasmeen Chana, Headteacher
Our safeguarding team is available to listen, support and take appropriate action where necessary.
If you believe a child is at immediate risk of significant harm, please contact the police on 999.
At CPS, safeguarding is not simply a procedure — it is part of our culture. We want every child to feel safe, heard, respected and protected so that they can learn, thrive and achieve.
